title: See who can actually work with AI, across both tech and business roles - July 2026 Updates - Codility
text:
July’s headline release:
see who can actually work with AI, across both tech and business roles
. Plus more releases worth knowing about.
See who can actually work with AI.
New AI-native tasks assess whether candidates can build an AI or ML system, or their critical thinking when an AI assistant purposely gets something wrong, the skill that matters more than knowing how to prompt.
Live now across Interview, Screen, and Skills Intelligence.
AI for Business opens assessment beyond engineering.
Every Codility assessment has run through a coding lens until now, which left business and non-technical roles out of reach, along with the AI-readiness skills every team is trying to measure. AI for Business is a different kind of task entirely: written, business-style problems on a simplified editor, with no code involved, scored through deterministic analysis against a defined answer key, not graded by an open-ended AI model.
Preview across Screen and Skills Intelligence. Enabled per account, ask your CSM or email
support@codility.com
The downloaded report becomes a complete record.
The PDF report has been thoroughly redesigned and upgraded, bringing VS Code solutions, integrity and proctoring summaries, code health, AI transcripts, skills evaluations, and the Excalidraw whiteboard into one faithful download.
Preview in Interview, included in the VS Code in Screen Preview. If interested, please contact your CSM or email
to learn more.
Skills Intelligence gets a broader integration system.
An expanded integration layer gives you Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, BambooHR, Personio, and 80+ HRIS integrations available in total.
Live for all Skills Intelligence accounts.
Interview environments add Next.js and R.
A dedicated Next.js environment brings server-side rendering and testable API routes to frontend assessments, and R closes a long-standing gap for data and analytics roles.
Live in Interview.
AI-Native Tasks
Live
Traditional coding assessments test candidates in a stripped-down editor, often with AI turned off entirely, the opposite of how engineers build now. AI-native tasks close that gap: candidates either build an AI or ML system themselves, or work alongside an AI assistant that’s designed to get things wrong sometimes, so the assessment can tell whether they caught it.
Why It Matters
One signal, two ways to test it: some tasks ask a candidate to build the AI or ML-based system itself; others embed an AI assistant as a co-worker that gets things wrong, sometimes on purpose, so the candidate has to catch it, the skill that matters more than knowing how to prompt.
The signal is judgment, not access: anyone can turn on an AI assistant. The harder skill is knowing when to trust it, when to double-check it, and when to overrule it, and that is what these tasks surface.
AI-optional by design: a companion set of project-style VS Code tasks ships alongside the same release, realistic multi-file work that stands on its own with or without an assistant enabled.
What’s New
First official batch of AI-native tasks live in packages, in Build AI and Work with AI styles
Work with AI tasks include deliberately seeded mistakes the candidate has to find and fix
AI-optional project-style VS Code tasks shipped in the same release
Coverage spans backend orchestration, data pipelines, debugging, and log analysis
Availability
AI for Business
Closed preview
Every Codility assessment has run through a coding lens until now, which kept the platform out of business and non-technical roles, and out of the AI-readiness skills every team is trying to measure. AI for Business is a new task type built for written, business-style problems instead of code, putting non-technical candidates in a simplified writing space with no code at all.
Built for non-technical candidates: tasks run on a simplified writing editor instead of the coding IDE, no engineering background required.
Deterministic, not AI-graded: scoring runs through language analysis against a defined answer key, not an open-ended AI model, the same rigor as the rest of the library.
Easy to find: a dedicated task library filter surfaces the AI for Business set.
New business-style task type across Screen and Skills Intelligence
Simplified editor built for non-technical candidates, no code involved
Deterministic scoring against a defined answer key, not open-ended AI grading
Preview. Enabled per account; contact your CSM or account manager to turn it on.
Codility Skills Intelligence
A Broader Integration System for Skills Intelligence
Skills Intelligence’s integration coverage has expanded, now live for every Skills Intelligence account.
Broader HRIS coverage: four connectors are active from the start, Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, BambooHR, and Personio, with 80+ HRIS platforms available in total.
Less manual upkeep: a configurable subset of employees syncs automatically and gets assigned to the right teams from your HRIS.
One place to manage it: a new settings page for connecting and managing integration providers.
Broader HRIS integration coverage available for every account
Four HRIS connectors active at launch: Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, BambooHR, Personio
New settings page for integration management
Live now for all Skills Intelligence accounts.
Codility Interview
The Downloaded PDF Report
The PDF report has been thoroughly redesigned and upgraded, so reviewers sharing a copy outside the platform get the same complete picture as the online report.
One faithful record, not two: VS Code task details, solutions, and environment context are now embedded in the PDF, with downloadable multi-file solutions for VS Code and basic IDE tasks.
Nothing left out: integrity risk, the integrity widget, full proctoring summaries, code health, AI Assistant and Copilot transcripts, follow-up questions, and skills evaluations now all appear in the download, alongside a new Excalidraw whiteboard section.
Easier to navigate: a redesigned header, overview, and table of contents.
Rebuilt PDF report layout with a table of contents
VS Code solutions and environment details included, with multi-file downloads
Integrity, AI, skills, and whiteboard content added to the download
Preview, included in the VS Code in Screen Preview. Contact your CSM or email support@codility.com to learn more.
Next.js and R Join the Interview Environment Library
Interview’s VS Code environments expanded to cover two gaps candidates and interviewers had run into. A dedicated Next.js environment now supports server-side rendering and API route testing, and R is available as a sandbox environment for data and analytics roles.
Frontend candidates get a production-like environment: server-side rendering and API routes are now testable directly in the IDE, where the basic editor previously limited or blocked some frontend and full-stack interviews.
Data and analytics roles get proper coverage: R was heavily requested, and now every feature already supported for other environments works for R too.
Next.js environment with server-side rendering support and testable API routes
R available as a sandbox environment in Interview
Live now in Interview.
Codility Screen
AI Follow-Up Questions and AI Candidate Feedback
Open preview
Both features move out of limited access and into extended Preview, available in every package with no separate enablement request.
Available in account settings, not a support ticket: turn either feature on yourself, no package change required.
Off by default: not every account permits AI use on the platform, so both features start disabled, and an admin chooses to turn them on.
Existing setups are unaffected: accounts that already had either feature configured keep their current settings.
AI Follow-Up Questions and AI Candidate Feedback available to every account
Available to enable and disable in account settings
Disabled in your Account Settings by default
Preview across Screen and Interview. Disabled in your Account Settings by default, available for every package.
Platform Improvements
Smaller releases that reduce friction across the platform.
Greenhouse integrations consolidate: Codility Advanced Screen and Codility Advanced Interview are now the single supported path for Greenhouse customers, with Harvest OAuth replacing legacy API key authentication. Legacy Greenhouse integrations and legacy Harvest API key authentication retire August 31, 2026.
Task details show the additional database services used in an interview: Redis, DynamoDB, PostgreSQL, and MongoDB now appear directly in task details when used. Available in Preview.
A roomier Interview interface: visual updates across Interview give more usable space and a more consistent layout, with no change to functionality.
A richer Sessions API: GET /api/sessions/ now offers three new opt-in fields, explicit session status, proctoring signals, and invite expiration date, with the inviter included by default.
Session export in Skills Intelligence: program owners and admins can export assessment session data directly from the platform, no more requesting a data pull.
